images.title: Move units, keep the total
images.purpose: Give a compact recap of levelling bars: move units from a tall bar to a short one, the total stays the same and the common level is the mean.
images.composition: A before picture on the left and an after picture on the right, joined by one arrow, with the calculation centred below; generous white space.
exact_structure: Left, labelled Before: exactly 3 teal (#0072B2) bars made of unit squares, with 2, 6 and 4 squares from left to right; the top 2 squares of the 6 bar are amber (#E69F00), and a curved grey (#6B7280) arrow carries them to the top of the 2 bar.
A straight arrow points from the Before picture to the After picture.
Right, labelled After: exactly 3 equal bars of 4 unit squares each, in teal with the 2 moved squares still amber on the first bar, and a reddish purple (#CC79A7) dashed line along their tops.
Centred under both pictures: Total 12 stays the same, and below it 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
Arithmetic check for the reviewer only, NOT drawn in the frame: 2 + 6 + 4 = 12 and 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
rejection: a different number of unit squares before and after (12 each)
any bar values other than 2, 6, 4 before and 4, 4, 4 after
images.takeaway: Levelling moves units without changing the total, and the level reached is the mean.
images.description: Three teal bars of 2, 6 and 4 squares become three bars of 4 squares after two amber squares move, with Total 12 stays the same and 12 ÷ 3 = 4 below.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Have students count the squares before and after to see the total is unchanged before using the bar leveller.

image_decisions.why: A before and after recap of levelling prepares students for the bar leveller practice.
